subject.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue

question: Should command-lane starvation aging preserve fresh foreground/user priority over aged normal/default work, or may aged lower-priority work overtake foreground after the threshold?
rationale: The ranking and fixed threshold define a scheduler policy for existing sessions under contention, and the current implementation contradicts the PR's stated foreground-preserving contract.

options.title: Repair foreground-preserving aging
options.body: Cap or rank aging so aged normal/default work cannot beat fresh foreground, then add the missing regression and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Accept stronger anti-starvation
options.body: Allow aged work to overtake foreground, but update the PR body, comments, tests, and linked issue triage to state that latency tradeoff clearly.

options.title: Defer to broader scheduler design
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want aging, foreground reservation, and gateway fairness policy decided together with the adjacent scheduler work.

recommendation.title: Repair foreground-preserving aging
recommendation.body: Cap or rank aging so aged normal/default work cannot beat fresh foreground, then add the missing regression and real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest queue and adjacent scheduler-policy history among the likely owners.
